comment: Engines the Engine Advisor knows about. 'forge_support' is what Twine Forge can build today: supported (has an adapter in tools/engines/), planned, or not-planned. Feature fit: yes | partial | no.

features.free_movement: Free movement on a tile map or open world
features.sprites_layered: Layered character sprites and transitions (visual novel staging)

sugarcube.label: SugarCube 2 (Twine)
sugarcube.summary: Browser hypertext with a full macro language and JavaScript; Twine Forge's default.

notes.realtime_action: Possible as a small canvas/JS widget inside a passage; keep it short and turn-based where you can.
notes.sprites_layered: Portraits and backgrounds are built in; full VN staging needs custom CSS/JS.
notes.large_story: One HTML file holds every passage; past ~1,500 passages load time and editing suffer.
notes.mobile_app: Via a web wrapper (e.g. Capacitor) - not built by Twine Forge.

harlowe.label: Harlowe 3 (Twine)
harlowe.summary: Twine's default format; friendlier syntax, less scripting power than SugarCube.

ink.label: ink (inkle) + inkjs
ink.summary: A narrative scripting language that excels at large, reactive branching text; runs on the web (inkjs) or inside Unity/Godot.

notes.realtime_action: Through a host engine (Unity, Godot) that runs the ink story.
notes.large_story: Compiles to JSON and handles very large scripts well.

renpy.label: Ren'Py
renpy.summary: The standard visual-novel engine: sprites, transitions, voice, rollback; desktop/mobile first.

notes.web: Web builds exist but are heavier and less mature than desktop builds.

godot.label: Godot 4
godot.summary: A general 2D/3D game engine: anything real-time, at the cost of building the narrative layer yourself (or with ink/Dialogic).

notes.branching_text: Needs a dialogue plugin or ink; Twine Forge's script pipeline doesn't target it.
